newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Pakistan to free fishermen in goodwill move.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan to free fishermen in goodwill move.

text.p: India and Pakistan have agreed to release each other's fishermen held in the two countries in a gesture of goodwill decided at bilateral talks on Wednesday, Indian officials said.
The foreign ministers of the two countries decided that the fishermen would be released as part of an effort to address humanitarian issues between the two countries, they said.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and his Pakistani counterpart, Gohar Ayub Khan, committed themselves at talks on Wednesday morning to continuing comprehensive engagements with each other to ease tensions on the subcontinent. It was the first formal meeting between diplomats of the two countries in three years.
"It was also decided that humanitarian issues between the two countries would be addressed urgently," the spokesman said.
Indian officials said the first move would involve the coordinated release of several hundred fishermen held by the countries for illegally fishing in each other's waters.

Last month, ahead of the resumption of high-level bilateral peace talks, Pakistan announced it would free 38 Indian children held along with adult fishermen as a unilateral goodwill gesture. Islamabad said it would release all Indian fishing boats and their crew seized in its waters if India reciprocated.
